title: Data Classes knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Data Classes”?
options: It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
A data class generates value-oriented methods from primary-constructor properties; `copy()` is shallow and shared referenced objects remain shared.
questions.answer_key: A data class generates value-oriented methods from primary-constructor properties; `copy()` is shallow and shared referenced objects remain shared.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: A data class generates value-oriented methods from primary-constructor properties; `copy()` is shallow and shared referenced objects remain shared. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Data Classes”?
options: Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Data Classes”?

Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
questions.answer_key: A data class copy recursively duplicates every object referenced by its properties.
